neighbours.label: the object or addressee of a heartfelt declaration of love, thanks, praise or hatred: the pronoun or the comma after the vocative ('I love ⟦him⟧ for it', 'Thank you, God⟦,⟧', 'HATE ⟦it⟧'); the slot where 'dearly / sincerely / truly' could follow
fire: My brother drove six hours to help us move, and I love him for that.
We thank you, heavenly Father, for the food on this table.
She stayed up all night with our sick daughter, and I adore her for it.
Bless you, O God, for the mercy you have shown this family.
My teacher never gave up on me, and I thank her with all my heart.
I despise this job. I really, truly hate it with every bone in my body.
We praise thee, O Lord, and we give thanks for this day.
To everyone who donated to the shelter this winter: thank you, all of you, so much.
quiet: My brother drove six hours to help us move, and I paid him for the fuel.
We told you, Mr Harris, about the food order for this table.
She stayed up all night with our sick daughter, and I relieved her at dawn.
Listen, Oliver, to the plan we have drawn up for this family.
My teacher never gave up on me, and I met her again at a reunion.
I left this job. I really did quit it after the second week.
We asked them, on Monday, to send the invoice for this day.
To everyone who donated to the shelter this winter: receipts for all of you are in the post.

notes: The − pole's output promotes ' sincerely', ' Truly', ' thank', ' dearly'. Probes: 'I love her for…' 0.73, 'We praise you, O Lord,' 0.71, 'Thank you, friends,' 0.39, 'hate it' 0.29; the same pronoun after a neutral verb 0.05, a neutral vocative 0.01.
